# Basis parameters

Every assumption the engine makes is a parameter of the **basis**: the defaults below, changed in the *Scenario & basis* panel, in a province file's `basis`, or in an experiment's `base` and arms. The whole set is hashed into the **basis hash** printed on every export, so a result can always be traced to what it assumed.

A province file only needs the parameters it changes. The editor completes each name and shows its meaning, range and default on hover, from the same source as this page. A value outside the range a file may set is left out, with a warning in **Problems**, and the rest of the file is applied.

Where each default comes from is in [Assumptions and provenance](../model/assumptions.md).

## The run

| Parameter | Meaning | Default | A file may set |
|---|---|---|---|
| `seed` | The province's seed: the same seed and basis give the same households, the same weather and the same history, on any machine. In a province file it is `seed`, beside the basis; an experiment chooses its own seeds. | `"agincourt-12"` | any text (a province file's `seed`) |
| `startDate` | The first day of the run (YYYY-MM-DD). | `"2026-01-04"` | a date, `YYYY-MM-DD` |
| `placeName` | The original village (Ebenezer): its name carries into the first city's institutions. | `"Ebenezer"` | a short text (60 characters at most) |
| `regionName` | The province the three cities, the centre and the airport make up: names the Mutual Bank, the burial society and the Hyperline. | `"Unity"` | a short text (60 characters at most) |
| `journalRetentionMonths` | Months of full journal kept in memory (older months keep their digests and ledger balances). | `36` | not settable from a file |

## Population and households

| Parameter | Meaning | Default | A file may set |
|---|---|---|---|
| `households` | Households seeded in Ebenezer, the original village, at the start. Every other settlement seeds the count its layout gives it, so the default province starts with 100 households. | `12` | 1 to 16 |
| `meanHouseholdSize` | Mean household size (Poisson-ish, min 1). | `4.2` | 1.5 to 7 |
| `ageProfile` | The mix of household types at the start (families, couples, single parents, multigenerational, elderly, single): young, balanced or ageing. The low-income settlements always start young. | `"balanced"` | `young`, `balanced`, `ageing` |
| `maleShareAtBirth` | Share male at birth (SA ≈ 0.503). | `0.503` | 0.45 to 0.55 |
| `educationMix` | Adult education attainment mix at t0 (sums to 1). Ebenezer's households only: every other settlement takes its tier's value (see Settlement tiers below). | none 0.03, primary 0.15, secondary 0.32, matric 0.3, tertiary 0.16, postgrad 0.04 | six shares, normalised to sum to 1 |
| `homeschoolShare` | Share of school-age children homeschooled (household-level decision). | `0.15` | 0 to 1 |
| `tertiaryProgression` | Probability a matriculant goes on to tertiary study (leaves for the city). | `0.35` | 0 to 1 |
| `youthEmigrationHazard` | Annual emigration hazard for a 18-30 year old (study / work elsewhere). | `0.05` | 0 to 0.5 |
| `immigrationHazard` | Annual probability an empty house is re-let to an in-migrant household. | `0.25` | 0 to 1 |
| `retirementAge` | Retirement age. | `65` | 55 to 75 |

## Mortality

| Parameter | Meaning | Default | A file may set |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mortalityPreset` | The mortality table the province lives on and A/E is measured against (see the presets below). | `"sa-2024"` | `sa-2024`, `agincourt-2005-07`, `agincourt-1994-97`, `developed-2020` |
| `mortalityImprovement` | Annual mortality improvement applied to the whole table (Lee–Carter-style drift). | `0.01` | 0 to 0.03 |
| `bereavementMultiplier` | Widowhood effect: relative mortality in the first year after losing a spouse. | `1.6` | 1 to 3 |
| `povertyMortalityMultiplier` | Extra mortality multiplier for households below the poverty line. | `1.15` | 1 to 2 |

### Mortality presets

Each preset is a Heligman–Pollard law with its own parameters for men and women. The life expectancies, infant and under-five mortality are what each table implies before any improvement (a period life table on the preset, radix 100,000, a₀ = 0.1), computed by the engine's own functions.

| `mortalityPreset` | Table | e₀ men / women | e₆₅ men / women | q₀ men / women (‰) | Under-five, men / women (‰) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `sa-2024` | South Africa 2024 (Stats SA calibrated) | 63.6 / 69.2 | 13.4 / 16.5 | 24.6 / 21.3 | 26.9 / 26.0 |
| `agincourt-2005-07` | Rural SA, early ART era (Agincourt 2005-07) | 50.8 / 55.8 | 13.4 / 15.8 | 32.5 / 40.3 | 43.8 / 53.1 |
| `agincourt-1994-97` | Rural SA, pre-HIV peak (Agincourt 1994-97) | 65.5 / 70.7 | 15.3 / 16.3 | 12.6 / 16.7 | 20.5 / 25.8 |
| `developed-2020` | Developed country, illustrative (e0 ≈ 79/84) | 79.0 / 83.9 | 18.5 / 21.5 | 4.4 / 3.6 | 5.2 / 4.4 |

Their sources, and the parameters themselves:

| Preset | Source | Fitted to | Men: A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H | Women: A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `sa-2024` | HP shape from Agincourt HDSS 2005-07 (Sharrow et al. 2013) re-calibrated to Stats SA P0302 2024: e0 M 63.6 / F 69.2, IMR 22.9‰ | single-year q | 0.0122, 0.7754, 0.6774, 0.005906, 3.4, 38, 0.0001256, 1.0885 | 0.01561, 0.8563, 0.5009, 0.005869, 2.6, 40, 0.00001868, 1.1092 |
| `agincourt-2005-07` | Sharrow et al. 2013, Demographic Research 29:39, Table 2 posterior medians | n-year interval q (1q0, 4q1, 5qx), converted to single years | 0.0262, 0.7754, 0.2083, 0.1199, 3.7761, 42.261, 0.0009, 1.0827 | 0.0356, 0.8563, 0.2373, 0.0867, 2.5266, 40.6617, 0.0001, 1.1092 |
| `agincourt-1994-97` | Sharrow et al. 2013, Demographic Research 29:39, Table 2 posterior medians | n-year interval q (1q0, 4q1, 5qx), converted to single years | 0.0106, 0.7829, 0.0855, 0.0243, 5.2779, 45.2412, 0.001, 1.0798 | 0.0148, 0.7852, 0.1048, 0.0126, 14.5269, 31.1959, 0.0003, 1.0958 |
| `developed-2020` | Illustrative HP parameters in the range reported for low-mortality populations; calibrated to e0 79.0 / 84.0, IMR 4‰ | single-year q | 0.0003348, 0.03, 0.1108, 0.001029, 9, 22, 0.00001774, 1.107 | 0.0003268, 0.03, 0.1013, 0.000001, 9, 22, 0.000008405, 1.112 |

## Health

| Parameter | Meaning | Default | A file may set |
|---|---|---|---|
| `healthProfile` | The health setting: South African rural or urban, or a developed country. It sets the prevalence of chronic conditions at the start (HIV prevalence is a tenth higher in sa-rural); developed also lowers the infection rates, maternal mortality and the chance of finding work. | `"sa-rural"` | `sa-rural`, `sa-urban`, `developed` |
| `hivEnabled` | Extra: enable HIV dynamics in the health profile. | `true` | `true` or `false` |
| `careQuality` | Clinic care quality: reduction in case-fatality for treated illness. | `0.55` | 0 to 1 |
| `fluAttackRate` | Seasonal flu attack rate per person per year. | `0.12` | 0 to 0.5 |

## Fertility, courtship and marriage

| Parameter | Meaning | Default | A file may set |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fertilityShape` | The shape of the age-specific fertility schedule, scaled to the TFR (see the shapes below). | `"sa"` | `sa`, `late` |
| `tfr` | Target total fertility rate for the ASFR level. | `2.41` | 0.8 to 6 |
| `contraceptionShare` | 0..1 share of couples deliberately spacing / limiting (scales the level). | `0` | 0 to 1 |
| `marriageAgeM` | Mean age at first marriage, men; the courtship hazard peaks a year before it. | `30` | 20 to 45 |
| `marriageAgeF` | Mean age at first marriage, women; the courtship hazard peaks a year before it. | `27` | 18 to 42 |
| `courtshipHazard` | Annual probability an eligible single starts a courtship (at the peak age). | `0.28` | 0 to 1 |
| `divorceHazard` | Annual divorce hazard for a married couple. | `0.006` | 0 to 0.1 |

### Fertility shapes

Births per 1,000 women a year by age band, as the shapes are written. The engine scales the chosen shape so that its total fertility equals `tfr` (the default 2.41), then adjusts each woman's monthly chance for her partnership, parity, schooling and health.

| Band | `sa` | `late` |
|---|---|---|
| 15-19 | 60 | 10 |
| 20-24 | 120 | 45 |
| 25-29 | 118 | 90 |
| 30-34 | 88 | 105 |
| 35-39 | 50 | 60 |
| 40-44 | 15 | 13 |
| 45-49 | 3 | 1 |
| TFR as written | 2.27 | 1.62 |

## Society, safety and getting about

| Parameter | Meaning | Default | A file may set |
|---|---|---|---|
| `churchAttendance` | Share of residents at the Sunday service in a typical week, and the mean of each person's faith, in the church-going cities (Emmaus and Ithemba; Newhaven has no church). Households decide together, so realised attendance tracks it closely. | `0.95` | 0 to 1 |
| `intrudersPerYear` | Expected intruder / external incidents per year. | `6` | 0 to 60 |
| `disputeRate` | Expected disputes per 100 residents per year before personality effects. | `25` | 0 to 200 |
| `policeEffectiveness` | Police response speed multiplier (1 = normal). | `1` | 0 to 2 |
| `carOwnership` | Chance that a household with a driver has a car at the start, raised by 30% above R15,000 a month of income and cut by 40% below it. Ebenezer's households only: every other settlement takes its tier's value (see Settlement tiers below). | `0.6` | 0 to 1 |
| `roadAccidentPer1000Km` | Road accident hazard per 1,000 km driven (injury or worse). | `0.0035` | 0 to 0.05 |
| `trainMach` | The Hyperline's cruising speed in Mach. The trains are launched and caught electromagnetically within the platform's length, so a hop between stations takes about a second of simulated time at Mach 5. | `5` | 1 to 12 |
| `climate` | The climate normals the daily weather is drawn around (see the climates below). | `"highveld"` | `highveld`, `western-cape`, `kzn-coast`, `temperate-north` |

|---|---|
| `highveld` | Highveld (Johannesburg) |
| `western-cape` | Western Cape (Stellenbosch) |

## Settlement tiers

Each settlement belongs to a wealth tier, and its households start from the tier's profile: schooling, cars, cover, savings and work. Ebenezer's own households read the baseline parameters above instead (`educationMix`, `carOwnership` and the cover shares, whose defaults are the `middle` profile's values), and open with 0.5 to 6 months of income in savings, although its tier is `affluent`. How many households each settlement starts with is part of its layout, not its tier. A file may set the shares marked *settable*, tier by tier, under `basis.tiers`:

```json
"basis": { "tiers": { "low-income": { "funeralCoverShare": 1 } } }
```

| Field | Meaning | `ultra` | `affluent` | `comfortable` | `middle` | `working` | `low-income` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `carOwnership` | Chance that a household with a driver has a car at the start, scaled by income as `carOwnership` above. *Settable.* | 0.98 | 0.95 | 0.85 | 0.6 | 0.32 | 0.15 |
| `secondCarShare` | Share of a household's further adult drivers (beyond the first) who run a car of their own. *Settable.* | 0.85 | 0.55 | 0.3 | 0.12 | 0.04 | 0.01 |
| `funeralCoverShare` | Share of households with funeral cover at the start. *Settable.* | 0.9 | 0.85 | 0.8 | 0.75 | 0.7 | 0.65 |
| `lifeCoverShare` | Share of households with life cover at the start. *Settable.* | 0.9 | 0.75 | 0.55 | 0.35 | 0.2 | 0.12 |
| `medicalAidShare` | Chance of a medical scheme at the start, scaled by income as `medicalAidShare` above. *Settable.* | 0.97 | 0.85 | 0.6 | 0.3 | 0.1 | 0.04 |
| `unemployment` | Share of working-age adults without formal work at t0 (drives the fallback job mix). *Settable.* | 0.03 | 0.08 | 0.12 | 0.3 | 0.35 | 0.42 |
| `savingsMonths` | Opening savings in months of household income, [lo, hi] uniform. | 12 to 48 | 4 to 18 | 2 to 10 | 0.5 to 6 | 0.3 to 4 | 0.2 to 2.5 |

Schooling at the start, by tier (shares of adults):

| Tier | none | primary | secondary | matric | tertiary | postgrad |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ultra` | 0.002 | 0.008 | 0.05 | 0.2 | 0.45 | 0.29 |
| `affluent` | 0.005 | 0.02 | 0.1 | 0.295 | 0.4 | 0.18 |
| `comfortable` | 0.01 | 0.06 | 0.22 | 0.36 | 0.28 | 0.07 |
| `middle` | 0.03 | 0.15 | 0.32 | 0.3 | 0.16 | 0.04 |
| `working` | 0.05 | 0.2 | 0.4 | 0.26 | 0.08 | 0.01 |
| `low-income` | 0.09 | 0.28 | 0.4 | 0.19 | 0.035 | 0.005 |

## Inputs with fields of their own

Two inputs are not set through `basis`, because they are not single numbers:

- **A mortality table** to live on instead of the preset: a province file's `mortality` (a CSV in the workspace, or a table inline), an experiment's `baseMortality` or an arm's `mortality`. See [Mortality tables](../workbench/mortality-tables.md).
- **Timed shocks**: `shocks` (at most 12), each a `mortality`, `repo` or `oil` shock over a span of months. See [Province files](../workbench/province-files.md#shocks).

Both are hashed into the basis like any parameter when they are present, and absent otherwise, so a default province's basis hash does not depend on them.
